decisions.rationale: No thesis threshold is breached on fact-sheet figures: operating margin 14.9%, FCF margin 15.3%, ROIC 11.9% and net cash. The net-cash trigger's statistics check likely read a gross debt ratio, so it is restated as a text trigger on the balance sheet. Evidence is unchanged since the BUY; hold at current size.

Fundamentals are improving and the franchise is sound, but the price has run ahead: the reverse DCF needs above-framework growth and the mechanical fair value sits below the price. The skew is balanced, not compelling, so hold at the conviction-3 size rather than add.

Fundamentals keep improving and the stock still trades below its own 5-year minimum cash multiples with modest upside to base fair value; no new evidence since the 2026-11-08 HOLD. Not an ADD: discount is moderate, there is no trend strength, and the position is at its conviction size.

Evidence is unchanged from the last review: quality and balance sheet intact, multiples below 5-year floors, the ROIC dip explained by inventory timing while margins hold. The guidance cut and discounting keep the score in the hold band, not at the buy threshold, so no ADD; the position stays at its current size.

Fundamentals and valuation are attractive, but a price fall alone is never a reason to buy: the cause of the 2026-11-12 drop is unknown and Q3 results are due Nov 25, 2026. Until results or a filing show the business intact, the evidence does not support high conviction. Cash is acceptable.

The fall is driven by the CEO's sudden resignation and a board investigation, not results; earnings land on 17 Nov. Until leadership and the investigation are resolved the risk is unpriceable, and the price sits above the mechanical base fair value. Governance veto caps conviction at 3: AVOID, no position.

The dip has a cause (guidance cut, CFO exit) that raises credibility and leverage risk rather than being a pure overreaction. Valuation is deeply cheap, but quality is low, margins are falling and the balance sheet is stretched. The scorecard gives conviction 1: not a buy; re-check once a quarter shows guidance holding and leverage falling.

Exceptional margins and a clean balance sheet, but the moat is thin, credit is deteriorating and the price already assumes sustained high growth; the scorecard does not reach the buy bar. Cash is acceptable.

Cheap versus peers and in an uptrend, but returns have been positive for only one year, the moat is thin, regulation can shrink the market, and no fair value is computable. Good but not compelling: AVOID; cash is acceptable.

Quality and trend are strong, but base fair value sits barely above the close after a sharp re-rating, the margin step-up is one year old and partly cost-driven, and buybacks are now debt-funded. The scorecard gives conviction 3: good but not compelling, so AVOID (owner rule: high conviction only) and watch the entry price.

Strong balance sheet and cash conversion, but earnings sit near a cycle high, fair value is flagged unreliable and TRY country risk is unquantified. The scorecard does not reach the buy bar; good but not compelling, so AVOID.

Scorecard total 8 gives conviction 3: quality, direction and balance sheet are full marks, but the value-blend upside is only moderate, the moat narrow and the key risk medium (unread Q3, unknown country/HUF mix). Good but not compelling at this price, so AVOID; cash is acceptable.

Quality, cash conversion and momentum are real, but P/E above its 5y range and the reverse DCF already discount continued flow growth and First Eagle synergies; the probability-weighted value sits below the price. Good but not compelling at this level.

Quality and balance sheet are excellent and the trend is positive, but the price sits above base fair value and implies growth above what is reported, while the 3-month trend is weakening after a sharp run. Good but not compelling at this price; cash is acceptable.

Quality, direction and balance sheet are excellent, but valuation support comes only from trend strength, the base fair value is below the price, and a one-drug franchise at a 62.8x P/E carries a high de-rating risk. Good but not compelling at this price.

Quality, balance sheet and trend are excellent, but every earnings multiple sits above its 5y maximum, the price needs high growth, and the moat is unproven against a cyclical AI capex wave. The scorecard lands at conviction 3, below the buy bar; cash is acceptable.

Cheap against peers with an 11.26% FCF yield and a real uptrend, but earnings are commodity-driven and near a cyclical high, own-history multiples sit high in their ranges, and the mechanical DCF is too wide to rely on. Good but not compelling: AVOID.

The setup qualifies, but the ATR stop at 87.02 means 2:1 needs 166.77 within 8 weeks, with no results in the window and the stock already at its 52-week high and EV/Sales above its 5y maximum. The evidence does not support that target, so this is an AVOID. Cash is acceptable.

The setup qualifies mechanically, but the full reversal of the post-beat jump reads more like a rejected breakout than a healthy dip, the trend is extended far above its 200-day, and the target only meets the 2:1 minimum with no supporting level above it. Good but not compelling; cash is acceptable.

The drift setup is valid and the business is strong, but the honest target is the 52-week high of 769.98, well short of the roughly 890 needed for 2:1 against the 612.12 ATR stop. A sub-2:1 trade fails the owner's tactical rule; the stop is not tightened to fit. AVOID; cash is acceptable.

The price follows the Proofpoint cash bid, not a trend. The 2:1 target sits at the deal-capped 50.31 high, and a deal break would gap through the ATR stop towards 31.79. This is merger arbitrage, which is outside the owner's two tactical setups, so the trade has no clear edge. AVOID.

The setup is real, but reward:risk only works on paper. The 452.66 target is the bare 2:1 minimum, not a level the evidence supports. With RSI 82.3 and the price far above its averages, the 14.5% stop is likely to be tested before any drift. The edge is unclear, so we avoid.

The setup qualifies mechanically, but the jump is large relative to a modest beat and in-line guidance, the stock is extended (RSI 70, far above its 50-day), short covering may have done the work, and the 186.00 target was set at the 2:1 minimum rather than by evidence. Good but not compelling: AVOID.

The drift setup is real, but the honest ceiling is the bull fair value 94.77, short of the 100.56 a 2:1 plan needs from a 66.15 stop. Price is far above its 50-day with RSI 83.6, so the edge looks largely priced. The owner's 2:1 tactical rule makes this an AVOID; no size.
